text:
jess: quick sync — planning a mixed k6 + locust traffic replay against staging this Friday to validate the recent kv-cache change and the new batching heuristics. can folks who own telemetry, infra, and the replay dataset ack?

omar: ack from infra. what windows do you need? we should pick a weekday low-traffic window — recommended: Fri 03:00-05:00 UTC.

jess: that window works. target profile: 1000 rps steady-state during the 30m soak, with 15m ramp up and 15m cooldown. total run 60m. goal: catch any latency p95 regressions > 20% and CPU/GPU memory thrashing.

liam: can you paste the exact k6 job and the locust scenario you'll run? need to sanity-check against current staging autoscale settings.

jess: sure — k6 will drive the short-lived edge requests, locust will do longer chat-like sessions. commands:

```bash
# k6 edge burst generator
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 15m edge-burst.js --out influxdb=http://staging-influx:8086

# locust master (start on control vm)
locust -f locustfile.py --headless -u 500 -r 50 --run-time 30m --host https://staging.redwood-inference.internal
```

jess: locustfile will use the replay dataset kept in s3://staging-replays/2026-03-01/ with sticky user sessions.

sophia: telemetry team: we'll enable additional traces for the runtime kernel selection path during the test. tagging with test_id=ks-replay-176999 so we can filter. Also will capture token-level latency histograms.

omar: infra notes: two things — 1) staging autoscaler max replicas currently set to 40 for the runtime pool, might need bump to 60 for 1k rps. 2) make sure dedicated GPU nodes aren't scaled down during the run (we'll set a hold). I'll add a temporary override:

```yaml
# autoscale override
namespace: staging
pool: runtime-gpu
min_replicas: 20
max_replicas: 60
hold_until: "2026-03-20T06:00:00Z" # keeps through the run
```

omar: created infra ticket #INF-5929 and added permissions for locust control VM to access the s3 replay bucket.

liam: perf regression checks — what thresholds? also enable the profiling hook so we can capture a 60s perf profile if p95 crosses threshold.

jess: thresholds: p50 change > 40% or p95 change > 20% relative to baseline (baseline run from 2026-03-10). Errors: >0.5% 5xx rate triggers immediate rollback. On threshold breach, ops-bot should notify #eng-oncall and pause the run.

ops-bot: [automated] noted: oncall notify rule configured for test id ks-replay-176999. Alert hooks: #eng-oncall (pager), #eng-runtime (slack).

sophia: for profiling, I'll coordinate with research to enable kernel-level sampling. add this header in requests so tracing knows to persist: `x-test-id: ks-replay-176999`

jess: please also snapshot config flags: new-batching=enabled kv-prefix-cache=v2. we'll attach to the run artifacts.

liam: one more: can we run a 10m dry-run tomorrow at 03:00 UTC with 200 rps to validate wiring (no long sessions)? quick smoke to ensure no auth/s3 perms break.

omar: yes — I'll schedule the dry-run and leave infra override in place. expect small flakiness with autoscaler during the dry-run, but should be fine.

sophia: telemetry will be on for the dry-run too. i'll share the dashboard link when ready.

jess: thanks — ownership: jess (run lead), omar (infra), sophia (telemetry & traces), liam (perf checks & rollback decision). next actions:
- liam: create perf-checks PR + add profiling hook (due: tomorrow 12:00 UTC)
- omar: schedule dry-run and open INF-5929 details (done)
- sophia: create dashboards + trace filters (due: tomorrow 09:00 UTC)
- jess: upload final replay manifest and post run checklist to confluence.

sophia: +1. i'll ping when dashboards are ready :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [automated] dry-run scheduled: 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z. Notification will be sent 30m prior.

jess: perfect. if anyone spots a blocker feel free to @here — otherwise we'll proceed with dry-run and then the 60m on Friday. :rocket:
